messages:
emma-parttime: Hi folks  quick PTO/carryover question. I'm increasing from 0.6 FTE -> 0.8 FTE effective 2026-09-01. How do accruals and year-end carryover behave when FTE changes mid-year? Also worried about the performance review blackout in Nov.
claire-peopleops: Congrats on the FTE bump! Short version: accruals are pro-rated by FTE on each pay period. Carryover rules depend on FT status by Dec 15: if you're FT by Dec 15 you get the standard carryover cap; if not, carryover is limited (or requires an exception). We'll need your effective FT date to calculate exact numbers. :memo:
rob-payroll: To be concrete: for 2026 we calculate accruals on a per-pay-period basis. Example: 0.6 FTE accrues X, 0.8 accrues Y. We'll run a retro adjustment for the Sept cutoff so your accrual ledger shows the switch on 2026-09-01. Need employee ID in the HR form before 2026-08-20 payroll cutoff.
nate-manager: Manager note  please avoid scheduling long PTO during the review blackout (2026-11-22..2026-11-29). If Emma needs time off then, we should plan coverage or an exception.
emma-parttime: Can unused part-time PTO be converted to FT carryover? I have 5 unused days now and want to understand if I can carry more into next year.
claire-peopleops: Policy detail: part-time accrual carries forward as accrued balance, but the carryover cap is based on your FT status and the cap amount applies to the balance at year-end. If you're FT by Dec 15 and under the cap you keep it. If over cap or not FT by cutoff, you can request a one-time exception to carry extra days (submit by 2026-12-05).
emma-parttime: Also: if I work during the company year-end shutdown (2026-12-24..2026-12-31) at 0.8 FTE, do I still get paid shutdown days or are those pro-rated?
rob-payroll: Company shutdown days are paid if you're on payroll that day. For part-time, we pay the shutdown days proportionally to your scheduled FTE (we credit the same hours you would normally be paid for that day). If you switch FTE earlier in December, that'll affect the calculation. We'll provide an example in the payroll confirmation.
emma-parttime: One more  can I convert up to 2 unused sick days to PTO as part of the FTE change? I recall there's a medical conversion clause.
claire-peopleops: Medical conversions are only for documented medical cases (manager + HR review). Non-medical sick days don't convert. However we do offer a one-time discretionary conversion for role changes at manager+HR discretion (rare). If you want us to evaluate, submit the conversion request form with rationale.
hr-bot: Reminder: submit FTE-change form and any conversion requests by 2026-08-20 to avoid manual payroll edits.
rob-payroll: If forms miss cutoff we run a manual job, e.g.:
```
./payroll_tool --retro-fte-change --emp=EEM789 --eff=2026-09-01 --new-fte=0.8
```
Attach HR approval PDF.
nate-manager: Emma if you want, I'll pre-approve coverage for review week to minimize disruption. Please confirm your preferred blackout flexibility.
emma-parttime: Thanks all  filing the FTE-change form now and will attach emp ID. Appreciate the example script and the heads-up on deadlines.
